## A new Claude for the hardest jobs

Anthropic released Claude Fable 5.2 and Claude Mythos 5.2 on 9 November 2026. Both are meant for the most demanding technical work, and both sit on the same model. Fable is the copy with extra blocks on risky cybersecurity and biology requests, which is why Anthropic can offer it widely. Mythos is that model without those blocks. Only organizations the company has checked can apply for it.

If you already use Claude, the change is which model you call for which job. Anthropic says testers found the new versions communicate more clearly than earlier Fable and Mythos models, and that output is up to 30 percent faster than Fable 5.1 and Mythos 5.1. The company also lowered the price. For ordinary coding and knowledge work, the same announcement tells you to start with Claude Opus 5.5, which it calls its strongest daily model, and to move up only when the job is ambitious enough.

On an ordinary week the flagship is for work that can run for hours or days, and Opus is for the short mail. The two names, the results Anthropic reports, and the limit on those results decide whether a switch is worth making.

## One model behind two product names

Fable is the version a paid plan can open. Anthropic's announcement on 9 November 2026 prices it at $8 per million input tokens and $40 per million output tokens, down from $10 and $50 for Fable 5.1, with an optional fast mode at $16 and $80 that can generate tokens up to 2.5 times faster, on Pro, Max, Ultra, Team, and Enterprise plans and as claude-fable-5-2 on the Claude API, AWS, Google Cloud, and Microsoft. Eligible paid plans also get extra Fable usage during launch week.

Mythos stays behind an application. Cybersecurity teams apply through the Cyber Verification Program. Life sciences researchers apply through the Life Sciences Verification Program. On Fable, Anthropic says its classifiers block high-risk cyber work, including penetration testing and writing exploits, and most tasks in research biology. A blocked cybersecurity request is answered by Opus 4.8 instead. A blocked biology request is answered by Opus 5.

Its documentation lists a context window of 1 million tokens and a maximum output of 128,000 tokens. The context window is how much material the model can hold at once. The product page describes sessions running for hours, research in many steps, and analysis carried through to a finished document, spreadsheet, or deck. It also says the model takes on ambiguous problems for days, questions and checks its own work, and directs other agents. Software that carries out a series of steps is called an agent. In the apps, Anthropic says Fable can advise Haiku, Sonnet, or Opus, or hand the simpler steps to those smaller models. Start on Opus 5.5. Move to Fable when a higher effort setting on Opus still does not meet the job, and move down to Sonnet 5.5 or Haiku 5.5 when the job is smaller.

## Those feats come from Anthropic's tests

The striking lines in the 9 November 2026 announcement are results from Anthropic's own prerelease testing, not from a referee outside the company. Anthropic says the models helped its engineers finish software migrations that had not been feasible, designed three working electronic devices from scratch, solved two open problems in black-hole physics, made substantial progress on robotics evaluations, and formalized the proof of Fermat's Last Theorem in 30 hours.

The device test and the proof are still the company's account. Anthropic says a one-paragraph prompt led the model to design a home voice-assistant hub, a USB speakerphone, and a handheld virtual pet, and that all three worked without electrical changes after the partner Diode built the boards. On the proof, Anthropic says about 1,000 Fable 5.2 agents finished a computer-checked formalization in 30 hours with little human help. An earlier formalization, with an unreleased research version of Claude and a human researcher, took 11 days. Opus 5.5, in the same setup of about 1,000 agents, had completed 26 percent after 18 hours, in a single run of each model. Both physics results, Anthropic says, concern black holes and the attempt to connect relativity with quantum mechanics, and both are written up as preprints. On robotics, the gains include tasks the model was not explicitly trained to do.

Safety testing is Anthropic's report too. The company says it ran extensive checks before release, including new evaluations for escapes from a sandbox. A sandbox is the restricted area that is supposed to contain the model. Anthropic believes the risk of high-stakes misalignment remains low. It says Fable's cyber and biology safeguards match Fable 5.1 and blocked about 55 percent less often in early use of claude.ai, Claude Code, and Cowork. It calls the protections against distillation the strongest it has shipped. Distillation is training a new model on a stronger model's answers. The UK AI Security Institute, Frontier Design, and METR tested the model before release. Anthropic points to its system card for their reports, so the announcement is not itself an outside verdict.

CNBC reported the same day that these are the first frontier models since chief executive Dario Amodei called in September for a slower pace of development, and that Anthropic is preparing a public listing that could come as soon as the following week. Anthropic has not confirmed that listing.

## Try Fable only on work you can check

If Fable is already on your plan, choose one hard piece of work whose quality you can judge. A long pack of source material that should become one document is a fair comparison. A two-line mail is not. Run that hard job on Opus 5.5 and on Fable 5.2, then keep the draft that needed less repair. Anthropic already names Opus as the daily model. A clearer or faster reply is a reason to look again, not a reason to move every task up.

Two limits belong next to whatever comes back. Cybersecurity and biomedical research may be refused on Fable, with a different model answering in their place. Mythos is the path Anthropic describes for checked organizations, and it takes an application. When you repeat a line about physics, a proof, or hardware, say that it comes from Anthropic's tests. The post does not include an outside rerun of those feats.

Launch week is a reasonable moment for that single comparison, on material that is not confidential, while the extra usage lasts. It is a poor moment to paste in customer files you have not tried this model on before.

> A faster flagship still waits for a hard job. The daily work stays on Opus.

November 2026 bei hohem Effort 45,3 Prozent erreicht, etwa gleichauf mit Opus 5.5 bei maximalem Effort mit 45,5 Prozent, bei ungefähr dem halben Preis je Aufgabe.

## Meta built a model for repeated steps

On 9 November 2026 Meta Superintelligence Labs released Muse Ember, which it calls its smallest and most efficient Muse model. It is built for the work agents repeat all day: calls to tools, coding subtasks, routing a request to the right step, pulling structured details out of text, and reading long documents. Software that carries out a series of steps is called an agent. Meta's point is that those repeated steps, not the one hard plan at the start, are where most of the cost sits.

That is why a cheap model is news for anyone whose company already lets an assistant work through a pile of files. Meta says Ember delivers more intelligence per dollar than Claude Haiku 5.5 or GPT-6 Luna at any reasoning setting, and that it matches Haiku's best score at about a third of the cost. On Meta's comparison, published the same day, Ember costs about $0.14 per Artificial Analysis task at an index score of 36, against $2.39 and a score of 37 for the larger Muse Spark 1.3. The intended pairing is in Meta's own line. Muse Wonder plans. Muse Ember handles the volume.

Whether that pairing is real at your company is a separate question from the chart. What still decides the choice is what the model can take in, which numbers are Meta's or a partner's, and where a rival small model still scores higher.

## Pictures and recordings sit in the same model

Ember reads text, images, audio, and video in one model, Meta says, so an agent can use a screenshot, a chart, or a scanned document, or start from a voice memo, a meeting recording, or a video, without calling a second model for that media. Meta also says it can operate a computer from screenshots.

Meta's post on 9 November 2026 sets Ember at $0.10 per million input tokens and $0.50 per million output tokens, with a context window of 1 million tokens and up to 512,000 tokens of output, on the Meta Model API and in Muse Code as muse-ember-1.0, and on Google Cloud and Oracle Cloud. Those token prices apply to prompts up to 200,000 tokens. Longer prompts cost more. The context window is how much material fits in one request.

TechCrunch's report the same day gives the split Meta is selling: in a customer-support agent, a heavier model sets the rules for an issue, and the light model applies them across tens of thousands of cases. Box says, in Meta's post, that Ember can score a contract against a negotiation playbook clause by clause and reach an overall risk rating, or screen candidates against a brief and flag borderline ones as alternates. Cloudflare says it ran up to 30 percent faster at the tail than the model Cloudflare compared, and that it handled investigations across several repositories. At the tail means the slowest replies, not the typical one. You.com says the 95th-percentile latency on its coding tests was 2.2 seconds, so 95 percent of those tests finished in that time or less.

Meta also says Ember is the first model it trained with Muse Wonder Full. TechCrunch counts it as the fourth Muse model, after Spark in April, Glimmer in August, and Wonder in October. TechCrunch calls Glimmer the open-source twin.

## The low price is Meta's comparison

The efficiency line is Meta's reading of results dated 9 November 2026, not a grade from a buyer. "More intelligence per dollar than Haiku or Luna at any reasoning setting" is Meta's sentence. The index comparison with Spark, 36 against 37 at about $0.14 against $2.39 per Artificial Analysis task, is Meta's table. Box, Cloudflare, and You.com are speaking about their own early tests, as quoted by Meta. None of that is an audit your company ran.

One public comparison cuts the other way, and it is the one to keep next to the price. On FrontierCode 2.0, where Artificial Analysis scores real engineering tasks by whether the change could be merged, Claude Haiku 5.5 scored 34.9 percent and Muse Ember 27.2 percent, in the results Meta published that day. A model can be cheaper per task and still be the worse choice when the output has to be mergeable code. Meta's post also includes scores from its own internal evaluations. Those are not the same thing as an Artificial Analysis number. Treat them as the lab's measurements.

Safety is Meta's account too. The company says it evaluated Ember under its Superintelligence Scaling Framework, including chemical and biological risk, cybersecurity, and loss of control, and that the model stayed below the framework's high-risk thresholds. It says the same testing asked whether Ember resists instructions hidden in web pages, documents, or tool outputs, and whether it asks a person before high-impact actions. That is a description of tests Meta says it ran. It is not a promise that every hidden instruction fails.

## Ask what the cheap model is allowed to do

The decision at work is which steps are allowed to run on the cheap model, and what those steps cost when the pile of documents is large. Ask whoever owns your assistant which model handles the repeated work, and whether that choice was made on price per task or on a test that looks like your files. Meta's 9 November 2026 list price is a vendor price for prompts up to 200,000 tokens. It is a starting figure for that question, not a quote for your contract.

If the job is code that a person has to merge, bring the FrontierCode result into the conversation. Haiku 5.5 beat Ember there, 34.9 percent to 27.2 percent, in the numbers Meta itself published. A support-style split, heavy model sets the rule and light model applies it, is worth asking about only if you already have a pile of similar cases. Use a non-confidential sample, and read what the light model flags before anyone acts on a risk rating or a candidate list.

Meta says it tested behavior on hidden instructions and on asking a person before high-impact actions. Your check is whether the product you actually use stops for a person on the actions you consider high impact. A low price does not answer that.

> A cheap model changes how much volume you can afford. It does not grade its own accuracy.

Meta says Ember understands text, images, audio, and video together. An assistant can look at a screenshot, a chart, or a scan, or start from a voice memo, a recording of a meeting, or a video, without a separate model for that kind of file. Meta also says the model can use a computer by looking at screenshots.

The examples Meta and TechCrunch give are all about applying one rule many times. ## The coding app is being used for other work

Google Antigravity began as an agent app for writing software. On 9 November 2026 Google said people are increasingly using it for other jobs as well: deep research, data analysis, drafting documents and presentations, prototyping designs, and automating everyday workflows. Software that carries out a series of steps is called an agent. Inside Google, the company says, tens of thousands of employees outside software engineering use Antigravity every week, across sales, finance, legal, product, design, research, marketing, and operations, alongside engineers.

Google's answer is not a second, weaker product. It is a second way to look at the same app. You can choose Knowledge Work or Software Engineering. Existing users keep Software Engineering unless they switch. Both layouts run the same agent, with the same frontier models, local files, plugins, skills, rules, custom agents, and MCP servers. MCP servers connect the agent to other programs.

The layout matters if the coding screen has been the thing in the way. It does not matter if you were hoping for a new skill the agent did not have yesterday. Google is explicit that software development stays at the core of the product.

## The screen changes, and the agent does not

Knowledge Work is a change to what you see, described in Google's post on 9 November 2026. Projects can sit on ordinary folders, including a conversation with no project, without a prompt to create a Git worktree or to pick a Git branch. Buttons that hand the work to an IDE are hidden. A worktree is a separate checkout of a code repository. You do not have to deal with one to start.

The conversation itself gets quieter. Instead of grouped tool calls and code diffs, with counts of added and removed lines, you see one live progress line. That line clears when the reply is finished. Permission prompts, the questions that ask whether the agent may do something, are summarized in plain language. The Overview panel stays hidden until there is something to show, then focuses on Documents, Artifacts, Links, Uploads, and Background Tasks. Files is renamed Folders. Review and Terminal leave that panel. Developer controls, including Terminal, workspaces, and detailed permission rules, move under Advanced Settings. Plugins you installed stay easy to see. Skills, rules, custom agents, and MCP servers keep running in the background.

New users meet a role question at first sign-in. The choices Google lists are Software Engineering, Knowledge Work, Data & Analytics, Science, and Design. The choice sets the starting layout, the starter prompts, and the plugins the app recommends. Picking a suggestion adds the plugin it needs and fills in the prompt.

The switch for someone who already has an account is Settings, then General, then Interface Layout. On a Mac that settings screen is Cmd and comma. On Windows and Linux it is Ctrl and comma. Google says the change applies immediately to open and new conversations, with no restart. Software Engineering remains the default for existing users.

## A calmer screen does not add a skill

The changelog for version 2.30.0, dated 9 November 2026, states the limit that the blog post does not lead with. The switch to Knowledge Work is not available on business and enterprise accounts yet. If you use Antigravity through work, the control may simply be missing. A personal account is the place the new layout can be turned on today.

What changes is the presentation. Google says the agent underneath is the same one, with the same models and the same connections. A plainer progress line does not mean the agent did less. It means you see less of the machinery. Plain-language permission prompts are still asking you to allow or refuse something. The summary does not decide for you. Google also says a tailored layout is a start, not a finished home for every kind of knowledge work, and that building software remains the core of what the app is for.

The same release finished the rollout of voice mode and of remote agents, which run a conversation away from your machine. That is a separate change. It is not what the new layout adds. The layout does not grant a capability the agent lacked.

If you use Antigravity yourself, outside a business or enterprise account, switch the layout and give it one folder that contains nothing confidential. Ask for a single document that summarizes what is in the folder. Then read every permission prompt before you approve it, including the ones written in plain language. The point of the trial is to see whether you can follow the work, not to discover a new power.

If the switch is absent, you are likely on an account the changelog excludes. Do not treat a missing menu as a mistake in your settings until you have checked that. Colleagues on work accounts will not see the layout just because you do.

If you cannot try the app, the part you can still use is the distinction. A calmer screen and the same agent are different claims. Ask anyone proposing Antigravity for a non-coding team whether the account type can select Knowledge Work, and whether a person will still read the approvals.

> The layout hides the coding tools. It does not shrink what the agent can reach.

Google's post specifies the Knowledge Work behavior. Folder-backed projects and a no-project conversation open without Git worktree or branch prompts. IDE handoff is hidden. Tool-call groups, inline diffs with add and delete counts, and subagent cards are replaced by one live progress line that clears when the turn ends. Permission prompts are summarized in plain language. Overview stays collapsed until output exists, drops Review and Terminal, renames Files to Folders, and centers Documents, Artifacts, Links, Uploads, and Background Tasks. Extensions remain when a UI plugin or an MCP app is active. Developer controls for Terminal, workspaces, and detailed permission rules sit under Advanced Settings. Installed plugins are surfaced. Skills, rules, custom agents, and MCP servers keep running.

First sign-in asks for a role: Software Engineering, Knowledge Work, Data & Analytics, Science, or Design. That choice sets layout, starter prompts, and recommended plugins. Accepting a suggestion installs the plugin and fills the prompt. Later, Settings, General, Interface Layout, reached with Cmd-comma or Ctrl-comma, applies immediately, with no restart.

## Work accounts lack this switch

Changelog 2.30.0, 9 November 2026, says the Interface Layout switch is unavailable on business and enterprise accounts. A missing control on a work seat is the documented state. Do not file it as user error before you check the account type. Personal accounts are the ones that can select Knowledge Work today.

Capability does not move with the layout. Google says the agent, models, and connections are shared. A single progress line and a plain-language permission summary reduce what the operator sees. They do not reduce what the agent can attempt, and they do not approve the action. The operator still has to read the prompt. Voice mode and remote agents finished rolling out in the same version. Note them as co-shipped, not as part of the layout. Google calls the layout a start and says coding remains the core.

## Confirm the account, then approve in the new wording

On a personal account, switch to Knowledge Work, point the agent at one non-confidential folder, and ask for one summary document. Read each plain-language permission prompt before you allow it. The check is whether the summary still names the action you think you are allowing. If it does not, stay on Software Engineering for that task so you can see the tool calls.

On a business or enterprise account, expect the control to be absent and do not plan a rollout that depends on it. Ask whoever administers the account whether 2.30.0 has an exception you were not shown. It does not, on the changelog's wording. If a colleague pitches the layout as a new skill for non-coders, separate the two claims: same agent, different layout, and no switch on work accounts yet.

> Same agent, less of the trace. Read the plain-language prompt before you allow it.

de.deepDiveMarkdown:
## Knowledge Work ist ein Ansichtsschalter, kein zweiter Agent

Googles Beitrag vom 9. November 2026 sagt, Antigravity, die Agent-App der Firma, werde über das Programmieren hinaus für gründliche Recherche, Datenanalyse, Dokumente, Präsentationen, Gestaltungsprototypen und alltägliche Automatisierung genutzt. Die Firma sagt, Zehntausende Googlerinnen und Googler außerhalb der Softwareentwicklung, in Vertrieb, Finanzen, Recht, Produkt, Gestaltung, Forschung, Marketing und Betrieb, nutzten sie jede Woche. Derselbe Beitrag lässt die Softwareentwicklung der Kern des Produkts bleiben.

Die Veröffentlichung ergänzt einen Schalter für die Ansicht. Knowledge Work und Software Engineering führen einen Agent aus, mit Frontier-Modellen, lokalen Dateien, Plugins, Skills, Regeln, eigenen Agents und MCP-Servern. Wer die App schon nutzt, bleibt auf Software Engineering, bis er wechselt. Googles Aussage ist Zugänglichkeit ohne Schnitt bei der Fähigkeit. Behandle das als die Beschreibung des Herstellers für zwei Ansichten auf demselben Agent.

## Ordnerprojekte, eine Fortschrittszeile, Freigaben in klarer Sprache

Googles Beitrag legt das Verhalten von Knowledge Work fest. Projekte auf Ordnern und ein Gespräch ohne Projekt öffnen ohne Nachfrage nach einem Git-Worktree oder einem Zweig. Die Übergabe an eine IDE ist verborgen. Gruppen von Werkzeugaufrufen, eingebettete Unterschiede mit Zählung von Ergänzungen und Streichungen und Karten von Subagents ersetzt eine laufende Fortschrittszeile, die verschwindet, wenn der Zug endet. Nachfragen zu Rechten werden in klarer Sprache zusammengefasst. Die Übersicht bleibt eingeklappt, bis es eine Ausgabe gibt, lässt Review und Terminal weg, benennt Files in Folders um und stellt Documents, Artifacts, Links, Uploads und Background Tasks in die Mitte. Extensions bleiben, wenn ein UI-Plugin oder eine MCP-App aktiv ist. Entwicklersteuerungen für Terminal, Workspaces und ausführliche Rechte-Regeln liegen unter Advanced Settings. Installierte Plugins werden nach vorn geholt. Skills, Regeln, eigene Agents und MCP-Server laufen weiter.

Die erste Anmeldung fragt nach einer Rolle: Software Engineering, Knowledge Work, Data & Analytics, Science oder Design. Diese Wahl setzt Ansicht, Start-Prompts und empfohlene Plugins. Wer einen Vorschlag annimmt, installiert das Plugin, und der Prompt wird gefüllt. Später gilt Einstellungen, Allgemein, Interface Layout, erreichbar mit Befehlstaste-Komma oder Strg-Komma, sofort und ohne Neustart.

## Geschäftskonten bekommen den Schalter in 2.30.0 nicht

Der Changelog 2.30.0 vom 9. November 2026 sagt, der Schalter Interface Layout sei auf Geschäfts- und Enterprise-Konten nicht verfügbar. Ein fehlender Schalter auf einem Arbeitsplatz ist der dokumentierte Stand. Melde ihn nicht als Bedienfehler, bevor du den Kontotyp prüfst. Private Konten sind die, die Knowledge Work heute wählen können.

Die Fähigkeit wandert nicht mit der Oberfläche. Google sagt, Agent, Modelle und Verbindungen seien gemeinsam. Eine einzelne Fortschrittszeile und eine Rechtefrage in klarer Sprache verringern, was die bedienende Person sieht. Sie verringern nicht, was der Agent versuchen kann, und sie genehmigen die Handlung nicht. Die Person muss die Frage weiter lesen. Sprachmodus und Remote Agents sind in derselben Version fertig ausgerollt. Notiere sie als mitgeliefert, nicht als Teil der Ansicht. Google nennt die Ansicht einen Anfang und sagt, Programmieren bleibe der Kern.

## Das Konto prüfen, dann in der neuen Formulierung freigeben

Schalte auf einem privaten Konto auf Knowledge Work, zeig dem Agent einen Ordner ohne Vertrauliches und bitte um ein zusammenfassendes Dokument. Lies jede Rechtefrage in klarer Sprache, bevor du sie erlaubst. Die Prüfung ist, ob die Zusammenfassung noch die Handlung nennt, die du zu erlauben glaubst. Wenn nicht, bleib für diese Aufgabe auf Software Engineering, damit du die Werkzeugaufrufe siehst.

Auf einem Geschäfts- oder Enterprise-Konto erwarte, dass der Schalter fehlt, und plane keine Einführung, die davon abhängt. Frag die Verwaltung, ob 2.30.0 eine Ausnahme hat, die dir nicht gezeigt wurde. Nach dem Wortlaut des Changelogs hat es sie nicht. Wenn jemand die Ansicht als neue Fähigkeit für Leute ohne Programmierung anpreist, trenne die zwei Aussagen: derselbe Agent, andere Oberfläche, und auf Arbeitskonten noch kein Schalter.

> Derselbe Agent, weniger von der Spur. Lies die Frage in klarer Sprache, bevor du sie erlaubst.
